feature: First-entry welcome letter for newly created characters

authorization.scope: Only new characters, once at their first entry into the game.
authorization.gift_selection: User delegated the choice of gift.

configuration.title: Vitej ve 4Story!
configuration.message: Vitej ve svete 4Story! Pro prvni dobrodruzstvi dostavas 5x Maly napoj zivota a 5x Maly napoj many. Prejeme prijemnou hru!
configuration.text_encoding: ASCII Czech text through the existing native NetString framing
configuration.item_evidence: Read-only live TITEMCHART lookup confirmed level 1, stack 30 and use value 600 for both templates. This verifies local item identity, not official reward balance.
configuration.eligibility: Character inserted while SQL settings are enabled, then first authenticated main-session entry with DB-loaded character, live registration and world grid. No existing-character backfill; no enrollment by login.
configuration.disabled_behavior: No new enrollment or preparation. Eligible characters first entering while disabled consume eligibility without a deferred gift. Already prepared letters continue recovery.
configuration.configuration_changes: Only affect letters not yet prepared. Pending payloads and operation IDs remain frozen.

durability.preparation: UPDLOCK/HOLDLOCK serializes concurrent first-entry preparation; immutable full native item snapshots and one operation ID commit before delivery acceptance.
durability.delivery: Existing Wolverine SQL transport accepts the frozen intent before welcome dispatch acknowledgement. Native header, both attachments and permanent TOperatorPostOperation receipt share the existing delivery transaction.
durability.recovery: Startup and actor timer recover unacknowledged SQL intents with the same ID. Repeated ready packets, relog, ambiguous acknowledgement, collection and deletion cannot allocate a second reward.
durability.entry_failure: SQL/transport failures leave the intent or eligibility available for retry without disconnecting a successfully admitted player.

history_review.result: Preserve authenticated character entry and main/secondary session admission. Welcome processing runs after successful playable entry, never from character-list/login requests.
Preserve teleport, pending transition, cast and state guards; welcome processing cannot turn an incomplete/secondary transition into an eligible entry.
Preserve tournament backup/admission handling; temporary tournament characters cannot issue the gift.

history_review.scope: Existing uncommitted quest/guild admission and SQL mail work
history_review.result: Keep quest recovery and guild-destination rejection before grid entry. Reuse durable operator-mail transport and receipts without changing existing reward IDs, item attributes or delivery contracts.

coverage: Real CONREADY actor entry, gift contents/native framing, duplicated ready and relog
Existing, DB-free, secondary, incomplete, unregistered and tournament characters excluded
Preparation/transport/acknowledgement failures retain one stable reward identity
Frozen pending payload ignores later configuration changes; stack splitting and invalid item charts
New-character trigger and concurrent SQL preparation; disabled-at-entry and deleted-character behavior
Native attachment transaction rollback, collection/deletion replay and permanent receipts
Immediate process exit after first entry without logout; repeated fresh-process recovery creates one letter with both gifts
Migration reruns preserve settings, identities and receipts
validation.sqlcmd_regression: Initial live migration attempt rolled back because sqlcmd defaults QUOTED_IDENTIFIER to OFF. Migration now explicitly sets required index options; the isolated runner repeats both migration passes with QUOTED_IDENTIFIER OFF.
limitations: No actual client mail rendering/claim/relog playthrough has been verified.
Process tests instantiate the real Map actor and SQL adapters; they are not a full MapWorker/WorldWorker restart journey.
This custom gift is not evidence that the incomplete Gameforge baseline or entire .NET port is complete.
